new.front: How do <bdi>إِعْرَاب لَفْظِيّ</bdi>, <bdi>مَحَلِّيّ</bdi>, <bdi>ظَاهِر</bdi> and <bdi>مُقَدَّر</bdi> fit together?
new.back: The first two divide all iʿrāb: <bdi>لَفْظِيّ</bdi> is on a <bdi>مُعْرَب</bdi> word's own ending, and <bdi>مَحَلِّيّ</bdi> only on the position of a <bdi>مَبْنِيّ</bdi> word. The last two divide the <bdi>لَفْظِيّ</bdi> kind: <bdi>ظَاهِر</bdi> is heard, and <bdi>مُقَدَّر</bdi> is implied, because the ending can't carry it.
new.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch.2 — class notes to 2026-10-13, revised 2026-10-22

new.front: What decides whether a word that shows no iʿrāb has <bdi>إِعْرَاب مُقَدَّر</bdi> or <bdi>إِعْرَاب مَحَلِّيّ</bdi>?
new.back: Whether it is <bdi>مَبْنِيّ</bdi>. In <bdi>جَاءَ الفَتَى</bdi>, the word <bdi>الفَتَى</bdi> is <bdi>مُعْرَب</bdi>: it has a ḍammah that its alif can't carry, so its iʿrāb is <bdi>مُقَدَّر</bdi>. In <bdi>جَاءَ هَذَا</bdi>, the word <bdi>هَذَا</bdi> is <bdi>مَبْنِيّ</bdi> on sukūn: it has no ḍammah at all, and only its position is in the place of <bdi>رَفْع</bdi>, so its iʿrāb is <bdi>مَحَلِّيّ</bdi>.
new.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch.2 — class notes to 2026-10-13, revised 2026-10-22

nahw-215.meaning: the iʿrāb a <bdi>مُعْرَب</bdi> word carries on its own ending, whether you can hear it or not — as opposed to the iʿrāb of a position
